title: Domain Modules vs. Function Wrappers — Check

questions.prompt: What is the primary job of a function in `netlify/functions/*`?
questions.explanation: The function files are thin wrappers handling HTTP plumbing; the decision logic lives in `netlify/lib/*`.
options: To implement the domain decision logic
To adapt an HTTP request to a `lib` call and serialize the result back
To define the Netlify redirect rules

questions.prompt: Keeping domain logic in pure modules lets most tests run without constructing HTTP requests or responses.
questions.explanation: Pure functions are tested by passing input and asserting output, avoiding the overhead and brittleness of request/response mocking.

questions.prompt: Which dependency direction reflects the inversion of control in this design?
questions.explanation: The wrapper depends on the module while the logic stays ignorant of the transport, so the host can change without touching domain code.
options: The domain module imports the HTTP wrapper
The wrapper imports the domain module, never the reverse
Neither imports the other; they communicate over HTTP
